title: Agents can self-verify against fixtures without waiting for Josh
description:
What: test/fixture infrastructure so agent work carries its own proof: golden fixtures for the nightly candidate shape, the kit install paths, and the packet verifier, runnable locally in minutes.
Why: verification currently bottlenecks on full gate runs (2.5-5 min each) and on Josh; cheap fixtures make the independent-verify gate fast enough to run daily.
Origin: reality-check phase 2; gate U / kit fixture patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture suites exist for all three surfaces, run green in under 5 minutes total, and the verify pass cites fixture results in at least one real bead closure.

title: Nightly stages carry hard budgets: tokens, attempts, wall clock
description:
What: per-stage budgets in the nightly driver (token ceilings per stage, attempt caps, 50-minute global budget already exists) with a budget-exhausted outcome class instead of silent fall-through burn; quota interactions stay with fr-fleet-quota-guard.
Why: reasoning models burn budgets invisibly; an unbounded stage is how a night dies quietly.
Origin: reality-check phases 1-2; token-floor lessons 2026-10-02.
acceptance_criteria: A forced over-budget rehearsal ends with outcome budget-exhausted and receipts show spend per stage; no stage exceeds its ceiling in receipts; budgets documented in RUNBOOK.md.

title: Graders never see the writer's receipts: independent grading isolation
description:
What: enforce grader isolation - the grading agent receives the packet and sources, never the writer's self-report, scores, or receipts; grading receipts record the isolation.
Why: self-graded work is how a 9.57 hid six deleted trigger phrases in the skills program; the same failure mode applies to packets.
Origin: reality-check phase 2; skills-program lesson (score is a false hope).
acceptance_criteria: Grading harness shows grader inputs exclude writer artifacts (logged manifest); a re-grade of one packet under isolation matches or explains differences vs its original grade; receipts cite the isolation manifest hash.

title: EPIC: one operating discipline across missions and agents
description:
What: umbrella for cross-mission discipline: merge protocol, skill-library conformance loop, refresh cadence, shared-state integrity, notification contract, self-verification infrastructure.
Why: two missions (franken, skill library) share one fleet, one Mac, and one operator; discipline that lives in one mission's habits does not protect the other.
Origin: /reality-check-for-project phases 1-2, 2026-10-03; Josh directives 2026-10-02..03.
acceptance_criteria: Epic closes when the morning skill-library review, the DAG burn-down, and the nightly loop run for 7 consecutive days with every discovered gap beaded and every child bead closed on cited evidence.

title: DAG work-pass time and instructions have no single canonical record (08:10 bead vs ~08:20 schedule)
description: Background: fr-m4x cites an 08:10 DAG work pass; the standing schedule recorded elsewhere puts the DAG work pass at ~08:20 and the DAG verify pass at ~16:20/16:40 in different records. Before the fr-m4x implementation there were no in-repo DAG pass instructions at all, so every pass re-derived its orders from chat context. Technical Approach: pick one canonical home (docs/dag-pass/MORNING-REVIEW.md in franken-research), record the agreed pass times, the step-zero morning review, and the burn-down/stop rules there; reconcile the VM cron schedules to match and cite the cron ids on this bead. Success Criteria: one in-repo document names each pass, its time, and its step order; cron list output matches it; fr-m4x acceptance wording and the canonical doc agree. Test Plan: cron.list output diffed against the canonical doc; a fresh agent reading only the doc can state the day rhythm. Considerations: changing cron times needs Josh-visible scheduling changes; DECISION beads stay parked.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical DAG pass doc and live cron schedules agree on times and step order; agreement evidenced on the bead.

title: EPIC: the nightly operating loop runs itself end to end
description:
What: umbrella for the self-sustaining nightly: census in, candidate built, independently evaluated, repo gates green, PR merged - no human touches the repo.
Why: reality check 2026-10-03: the loop shipped once with manual completion (PR #20) and once evaluator-green but gate-blocked. It is not yet self-sustaining.
Origin: /reality-check-for-project phases 1-2, 2026-10-03.
acceptance_criteria: Epic closes when fr-nightly-proof-week closes on 7 consecutive launchd nights with zero manual repo writes and every child bead is closed on cited evidence.

title: Morning reports still land when the VM cron worker dies on provider overload
description: What: the 07:20 franken-nightly report job (VM cron) failed 2026-10-03 on provider overload (529/engine_overloaded) before reading the Mac state; the report only reached Josh because an agent checked the Mac by hand. AGENTS.md records cron workers dying twice before. Make the report path resilient: the Mac driver already writes state/last-run.json and state/<date>-report.md; the delivery step needs a design that survives a dead reader (Mac-side digest artifact + thinner reader, or a local notifier).\nWhy: a nightly that silently goes unreported reads as a failed night; Josh should never have to ask whether it ran.\nOrigin: cron run e438c26f 2026-10-03 provider overload; prior cron deaths 2026-10-02.
acceptance_criteria: A report reaches Josh for a simulated dead-worker morning without manual recovery: evidence is a delivered digest produced from Mac artifacts (state/last-run.json + report.md) even when the VM reader turn fails; mechanism documented in RUNBOOK.md.
